samples.reference_class: Historical filovirus outbreaks declared by WHO
drivers_up: There is an active filovirus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, indicating the presence of the virus in the region.
Filovirus outbreaks, particularly Ebola and Marburg, have shown patterns of recurring emergence, especially in Africa.
The current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has a substantial number of suspected cases and deaths, suggesting a potentially escalating situation.
drivers_down: The ongoing outbreak might be contained effectively, reducing the likelihood of another distinct outbreak emerging by the end of 2026.
Global health measures and surveillance have improved since past outbreaks, potentially reducing the chances of a new outbreak going undetected until it is large enough to be declared by WHO.
samples.why_might_be_wrong: Surveillance and reporting mechanisms may either overestimate or underestimate the actual spread of filovirus, affecting the likelihood of WHO declaring a new outbreak.
samples.rationale: The base rate for WHO declaring a new filovirus outbreak in any given six-month period is relatively low, given the history of such events. However, the presence of an active outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with a significant number of cases and deaths, increases the probability of another outbreak emerging. While global health improvements could mitigate this risk, the historical recurrence of filovirus outbreaks in Africa suggests a non-trivial chance of a new outbreak declaration. Balancing these factors, the probability of WHO declaring a new filovirus outbreak distinct from the ongoing Bundibugyo event is moderately higher than the base rate.
